# Cross-repo dependency edges are silently dropped by the sync prefix filter

## Summary

A dependency edge whose target is a **foreign** (cross-project) work item id is
silently deleted during `wl sync`, so a recorded cross-repo blocker disappears
from the local store. The loss has **two** drop points — the merge-time prefix
filter and the store's destructive import edge guard — both of which must be
fixed for a cross-repo edge to survive a full or delta sync.

## Problem

A dependency edge whose target is a **foreign** (cross-project) work item id is
removed by the sync path, so a recorded cross-repo blocker can silently
disappear from the local store on a `wl sync`.

Discovered-from `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` (2026-11-26): recording the cross-repo
blocker `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5` (a `../SorraAgents` item)
with `wl dep add`, then running `wl sync`: the edge was present before the sync
and absent afterwards (`select … from dependency_edges where fromId=…` returned
no rows). A minimal reproduction is recorded in a comment on this item: the
store held two outbound edges — `→ SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5` (foreign target) and
`→ WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` (local target); after `wl sync` only the local-target
edge remained. Same condition, different outcome purely by target prefix.

## Users

The people and systems that must keep seeing a cross-repo block:

- **Producer / agent sequencing cross-repo work** — e.g. `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG`
  is blocked on this item and cannot reach `in_review` until a
  `../SorraAgents` item lands; its producer-chosen sequencing relies on the
  edge surviving sync.
- **`wl next`, the audit gates and the worklist** — must keep treating a
  cross-repo blocker as active until the foreign endpoint is resolved.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I record `wl dep add <local> <foreign>` and expect the block
  to still be there after `wl sync`, so I can sequence work across repositories.
- As an agent running `wl next`, I expect an item blocked on a foreign item to
  stay blocked (and to be reported as such) instead of silently becoming
  eligible.

## Root cause

There are **two** drop points. Fixing only the first (the item's original
pointer) still fails the round-trip ACs.

1. **Merge-time prefix filter** — `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts:82`:

   ```ts
   const keptEdges = edges.filter(e => allowedItemIds.has(e.fromId) && allowedItemIds.has(e.toId));
   ```

   `allowedItemIds` contains only the ids of pulled items that match the local
   project prefix (`isOwnProjectItemId`). A cross-repo edge's target id is by
   definition never in that set, so every foreign-target edge arriving from the
   remote is filtered out of the merged edge set.

2. **Destructive import edge guard** — `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts:227`
   (`importWorkItems`, used by the full-snapshot persist path in
   `src/commands/sync.ts` ≈ line 460):

   ```ts
   if (ctx.store.getWorkItem(edge.fromId) && ctx.store.getWorkItem(edge.toId)) {
     desiredEdges.set(`${edge.fromId}\u0000${edge.toId}`, edge);
   }
   ```

   `desiredEdges` only includes edges whose **both** endpoints resolve to a
   locally-stored work item. A `local → foreign` edge has no local row for the
   foreign target, so it is excluded from `desiredEdges`; the subsequent delete
   loop removes it from `dependency_edges`. The non-destructive delta path
   (`upsertItems`, ≈ line 329) has the same both-endpoints-local guard, so a
   *new* foreign edge arriving in a delta is not persisted (existing ones
   survive because upsert never deletes).

The merge itself (`mergeDependencyEdges` in `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts`) is a
**union** of local and remote edges and therefore preserves local foreign
edges; the loss happens downstream — on the remote side (prefix filter) and on
the persist side (endpoint guard). This also explains the repro's
"re-adding and syncing again kept it" observation: a delta persist
(`upsertItems`) never deletes, whereas a full persist (`import`) does (see
Appendix A2).

Foreign-edge support itself is intentional (`WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC`, parent
`WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD`; `wl dep add --help`: "dependsOn may be a foreign
cross-project id"), and `src/cross-repo/foreign-store.ts` reads the sibling
store read-only to display such edges — so both guards contradict the feature.

## Impact

Recording a dependency on another project's work item now actually holds — the
block stays visible after a sync instead of quietly evaporating.

## Why it matters

- A cross-repo blocker (e.g. "this item cannot reach `in_review` until a
  sibling repository's item lands") is unenforceable: it vanishes on the next
  pull, and nothing reports the deletion.
- Silent relationship loss is data loss: `wl next`, the audit gates and the
  worklist all stop seeing the block with no diagnostic.
- `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` is directly affected — its producer-chosen sequencing
  (Q2 = C: record the `../SorraAgents` skill switch as a blocker) relies on the
  edge surviving sync.
- Every operator using cross-repo dependencies (documented in
  `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md`) silently loses their recorded blockers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` keeps an edge when **either** endpoint is an
  allowed local item (equivalently: drops only edges whose endpoints are both
  foreign), pinned to the `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5`
  regression case.
- The store's import/upsert edge guard persists an edge when **either** endpoint
  resolves to a stored work item, so a `local → foreign` edge survives a full
  (`importWorkItems`) and a delta (`upsertItems`) persist; an edge is dropped
  only when neither endpoint resolves to a stored item.
- A cross-repo edge survives a full sync round-trip: `wl dep add <local>
  <foreign>` → `wl sync` (full snapshot) → the edge is still present in
  `dependency_edges` and still reported by `wl dep list <local>`.
- A cross-repo edge survives a delta sync between an ahead and a behind store,
  and is never resurrected after the local item that owns it is deleted.
- Loss is never silent: if any edge must be dropped during a merge/persist,
  `wl sync` reports the count and the affected ids (same visibility as the
  existing `Foreign-prefix filter: dropped N remote item(s)` line).
- The JSONL export emits a `local → foreign` edge on the owning item's
  `dependencies` array (round-trip guard) and the import re-hydrates it.
- Existing behaviour for foreign **items** is unchanged: foreign items and their
  comments/audit results are still never imported.
- Tests cover: the filter's either-endpoint rule, the import/upsert
  either-endpoint rule, a full sync round-trip, a delta ahead/behind sync, the
  delete-then-stale-remote non-resurrection case, and the dropped-edge
  diagnostic.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Two-stage fix, not one.** The prefix filter alone does not satisfy the
  round-trip ACs; the destructive import endpoint guard must be relaxed in the
  same change (see Root cause).
- **Existing test asserts the bug.** `tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts:120`
  ("drops dependency edges that touch dropped foreign items") currently expects
  `GUA-001 → WL-001` to be dropped; that expectation must be inverted (only
  both-foreign edges now drop).
- **Foreign items must still be dropped.** The prefix filter is
  defense-in-depth against cross-project pollution (`SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT`);
  only *edges owned by a local item* may survive, never foreign items,
  comments or audits.
- **Filter discipline is non-negotiable.** No path may import a foreign *item*;
  the fix must not weaken `isOwnProjectItemId` or the repo-context guard.
- **Backwards compatibility.** Same-project edge behaviour and existing sync
  output must be unchanged; the new diagnostic is additive.
- **Scope creep guard.** Related opportunities discovered during the fix (e.g. a
  general dependency-edge tombstone for `dep rm` resurrection) are logged as
  separate work items linked from this one, not folded in (see Appendix A3).

## Existing state

- `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` (`src/sync/prefix-filter.ts`) returns
  `{ items, comments, edges, audits, droppedItems }`; edges require both
  endpoints to be allowed.
- `importWorkItems` (`packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts`) performs a
  destructive differential replace; edges require both endpoints to be locally
  stored, and edges absent from `desiredEdges` are deleted.
- `upsertItems` (same file) saves an edge only when one endpoint is in the
  upserted batch **and** both endpoints are locally stored.
- `sync.ts` logs `Foreign-prefix filter: dropped N remote item(s) …` when items
  are dropped, but reports nothing about dropped edges.
- JSONL export embeds edges inside work items via
  `dependenciesFromEdges(normalizedEdges, item.id)` (`src/jsonl.ts`), so a
  `local → foreign` edge is already emitted on the local item's
  `dependencies` array; a `foreign → local` edge is never emitted because the
  foreign item is not exported.
- `getAllDependencyEdges()` selects all edges with no prefix filter.

## Desired change

- `filterRemoteDataByPrefix`: `keptEdges` becomes
  `allowedItemIds.has(e.fromId) || allowedItemIds.has(e.toId)`, and the result
  gains `droppedEdges: string[]` (e.g. `"WL-A->SA-B"`).
- `src/commands/sync.ts`: log a `Foreign-prefix filter: dropped N edge(s) …`
  line alongside the existing dropped-item line, mirroring its human/JSON
  visibility.
- `importWorkItems` / `upsertItems`: the endpoint guard becomes
  `getWorkItem(fromId) || getWorkItem(toId)`; a deleted local owner therefore
  drops its edges (cascade) and cannot be resurrected by a stale remote
  snapshot.
- `src/jsonl.ts`: add a round-trip guard test (no behaviour change expected —
  confirm the export/import path already carries foreign-target edges).
- Tests and docs updated as listed in the ACs.

## Key Files

- `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — the either-endpoint rule, the `droppedEdges`
  diagnostic and unit tests.
- `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts` — relax the both-endpoints-local
  guard in `importWorkItems` (≈ line 227) and `upsertItems` (≈ line 329).
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — surface the dropped-edge count alongside the
  existing dropped-item line (≈ line 267).
- `src/jsonl.ts` — round-trip guard for foreign-target edges on
  `dependenciesFromEdges` / `importFromJsonlContent`.
- `tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts` — invert the existing edge-drop
  expectation and add the `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWFFD9N0050SP5`
  regression case.
- `tests/database-transactional-import-next.test.ts` (or a new focused import
  test) — foreign-endpoint survival through `import`/`upsertItems`, delete then
  stale-remote non-resurrection.
- `tests/jsonl.test.ts` — export/import round-trip of a foreign-target edge.
- `MULTI_PROJECT_GUIDE.md` — note that cross-repo edges survive sync and that
  only fully-foreign edges are dropped (with the diagnostic).
- `docs/CROSS_PROJECT_POLLUTION_CLEANUP.md` — record that the merge-time prefix
  filter keeps local-owner foreign edges and reports dropped-edge ids.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — update the `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` row if the
  contract changes.

## Test plan

- **Unit — filter:** `filterRemoteDataByPrefix` keeps `local→foreign` and
  `foreign→local`, drops `foreign→foreign`, and reports the dropped pairs.
- **Unit — persist:** `importWorkItems` and `upsertItems` keep an edge with one
  local endpoint and one foreign endpoint; drop an edge with both foreign; drop
  the edge when the local owner is deleted.
- **Integration — full sync round-trip:** real temp repo, `wl dep add` with a
  foreign id, `wl sync`, assert `dependency_edges` and `wl dep list` still show
  it (`tests/sync-prefix-filter.test.ts` CLI section or a new
  `tests/cli/sync-cross-repo-edge.test.ts`).
- **Integration — delta sync:** ahead/behind stores; a foreign edge added on
  the ahead store survives the delta merge; deleting the owner then syncing a
  stale behind store does not resurrect it.
- **Diagnostic:** a sync whose remote carries a fully-foreign edge logs the
  count and ids; a sync with none logs nothing new.
- **Regression:** existing same-project edge behaviour and the foreign
  item/comment/audit drops are unchanged.

## Related work

- `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` (**Add a table for ACs**, epic) — **blocked on this
  item**; it needs the cross-repo edge fix to sequence the `../SorraAgents`
  skill switch.
- `WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC` (**Foreign dependency edge CRUD**) — the intentional
  feature this filter contradicts; foreign ids are supported as blockers.
- `WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD` (parent of the cross-repo feature) — discovery of
  sibling stores and foreign blocker resolution.
- `WL-0MVWEETA9006LFED` (**Cross-repo dependency documentation**) — the docs
  this fix must extend.
- `WL-0MM8V55PV1Q32K7D` (**Fix destructive `db.import()` in GitHub flows**) —
  introduced `upsertItems`; the same both-endpoints-local guard is the second
  drop point here.
- `SA-0MSC0BM1V0032UYT` — the merge-time prefix filter (defense-in-depth) being
  corrected.
- `WL-0MSAH26DD001XXST` — repo-context guard; unaffected, and must stay strict.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**A1 — Is this a genuine producer decision or a routine repo-search question?**

- Q: The item's root-cause pointer names only `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts`; is
  the import-store endpoint guard in scope?
- Answer (repo research, this intake): **Routine — in scope.** The ACs require a
  cross-repo edge to survive a "full sync round-trip" and a delta sync. A full
  `wl sync` runs the destructive `importWorkItems`, whose
  `getWorkItem(fromId) && getWorkItem(toId)` guard deletes any edge without a
  local foreign target. Therefore the import guard is a necessary part of
  satisfying the existing ACs, not new scope. Evidence:
  `packages/shared/src/database/import-export.ts:227`,
  `src/commands/sync.ts:460`.
- Outcome: recorded as Root cause #2, a Key File and a test-plan item; no
  producer hold.

**A2 — Why did the reporter observe "re-adding and syncing again kept it"?**

- Q: The bug description says the loss is non-deterministic ("depends on whether
  the remote snapshot carries the edge"); what explains that?
- Answer (repo research): The merge is a union, and the persist step differs by
  sync kind. A **delta** persist uses `upsertItems` (non-destructive — it never
  deletes, so an existing foreign edge survives), while a **full** persist uses
  `importWorkItems` (destructive — it deletes any edge absent from
  `desiredEdges`). Whether a given sync is full or delta depends on the delta
  cadence/watermarks (`src/commands/sync.ts` export decision). Hence the loss
  is intermittent. Evidence: `src/sync/merge-collateral.ts`
  (`mergeDependencyEdges`), `import-export.ts:227` vs `:329`.
- Outcome: captured in Root cause; the fix must cover **both** persist kinds.

**A3 — Does "never resurrected after the local item deletes it" mean
`wl dep rm`, or deletion of the owning work item?**

- Q: AC3's "the local item deletes it" is ambiguous.
- Answer (reasonable assumption): interpret as **deletion of the local work item
  that owns the edge**, not `wl dep rm`. Rationale: `deleteWorkItem` already
  cascades `dependency_edges` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:1356`),
  and the relaxed endpoint guard (keep iff *either* endpoint resolves) makes a
  deleted owner's edges unresolvable, so a stale remote snapshot cannot
  resurrect them. General `dep rm` resurrection on a stale remote snapshot is a
  **separate** pre-existing concern affecting all edges (not just cross-repo)
  and is out of scope here (scope-creep guard, Constraints) — logged as a
  follow-up if the implementer confirms it exists.
- Status: **assumption recorded, not a blocking question.**

**A4 — Does the "either endpoint" rule keep `foreign → local` edges too, even
though JSONL never exports them?**

- Q: The AC says "either endpoint"; AC text also says "dropping only edges whose
  local endpoint is itself foreign".
- Answer (reasonable assumption): the predicate is
  `allowedItemIds.has(fromId) || allowedItemIds.has(toId)` — keep if **any**
  endpoint is local. In practice remote edges are always `local → foreign`
  because `dependenciesFromEdges` only emits edges from exported (local) items,
  so the `foreign → local` branch is defensive only; it is harmless and matches
  the stated "either endpoint" intent. The redundant "local endpoint is itself
  foreign" phrasing is read as "neither endpoint is local → drop".
- Status: **assumption recorded, not a blocking question.**

**A5 — Duplicate-work check.**

- Command: `wl search` with keywords `cross-repo`, `foreign edge sync`,
  `dependency edge sync drop`, `dependency_edges import`.
- Answer: no completed item satisfies this item's ACs. Closest related items
  are `WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC` (foreign edge CRUD — introduces the feature, does
  not fix sync) and `WL-0MM8V55PV1Q32K7D` (non-destructive `upsertItems` — a
  different guard). No duplicate; no rewrite needed.
- Outcome: related work listed above.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MVWEENZL008XGYC** – Foreign dependency edge CRUD (completed)
- **WL-0MVWEEMP2002N37W** – Foreign dependency edge and isolation spec (completed)
- **WL-0MVWEETA9006LFED** – Cross-repo dependency documentation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, actually, add, adding (+161 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: absent, acceptance, actually, add, affected (+155 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: absent, actually, add, adding, again (+147 more)

# Cross-repo AC blocker contract

## Goal

Keep the Q2 = C sequencing guarantee enforceable and auditable: the cross-repo
blocker edge must survive `wl sync` once the prefix-filter bug is fixed, and the
compatibility contract that lets the skills keep parsing prose until
`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` lands must be written down in this repository, not only in
the intake Appendix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The cross-repo item is the recorded blocker: **`SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`** (*Use the worklog acceptance-criteria table instead of parsing AC prose*, `high`, `open`, `../SorraAgents`) switches the skills that parse AC prose (at least `find-related` and `implement`, plus the shared `tree_coverage.py` extraction) onto the table, and the dependency edge `WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG` → `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5` is recorded in this store, so this item cannot reach `in_review` until that item completes (producer decision Q2 = C). This item documents the compatibility contract that keeps the current description-based parse working until that item lands.
- A verification step asserts the edge is present via `wl dep list WL-0MWXBHODR002ZLJG --json` immediately before this item is marked `in_review`, and after `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` (foreign edges dropped by the sync prefix filter) is completed the edge is asserted to survive a full `wl sync` cycle.
- `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` records the three-step delivery sequence, the interim compatibility rule (prose stays the fallback; `wl show` falls back to it), and the statement that the blocker is repeated in prose in the parent description so it survives a dropped edge.
- The SorraAgents item is commented with the second-landing requirement it inherits: the fingerprint schema-3 lockstep (`_AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_SCHEMA` and `_compute_content_fingerprint`) and the accepted-schema-set transition window.
- No file in `../SorraAgents` is edited from this worktree; the only cross-repo action is a comment on the existing item through its own worklog store.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the contract section to `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` (shared with "AC docs and suite handoff" (`WL-0MWXJHCVR0056VMB`)) and the three-step sequence to `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md`.
- Add a small pre-`in_review` check script/snippet that verifies the edge (documented in the item comment, not a new CLI command).
- Comment the fingerprint lockstep requirement on `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` (critical: cross-repo edges dropped by the sync prefix filter) for the "survives sync" assertion.
- Related cross-repo item: `SA-0MWXFFD9N0050SP5`.

## Deliverables

- Documented compatibility contract and delivery sequence.
- Edge-presence verification recorded before `in_review`.
- Lockstep requirement commented on the SorraAgents item.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/acceptance-criteria.md` — compatibility contract section.
- `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` — delivery-sequence note.
- `src/sync/prefix-filter.ts` — read-only reference for the dropped-edge bug.

## Notes

- The edge is currently dropped on every sync (see the intake comment on the parent); the prose statement of the blocker is the authoritative record until `WL-0MWXIT6H3006TY2I` is fixed.
